Design and implementation of a major overhaul of a feature allowing Decathlon employees to checkout a customer without going to the register.

The feature includes:
- Cart composition
- Customer identification
- Bank card payment

Everything was handled: stock, invoice, security gates, loyalty card, and NFC bank card payment.

To guarantee high availability, the entire transaction was synchronised in real time on Firebase. Each transaction can be completed either by the employee or by the server, following the 2-way binding principle.

**Key challenges:**
- High payment processing resilience — every transaction produced a concrete, actionable result even when multiple services are called simultaneously
- Strong stability even in challenging environments (weak internet connection)
- Easy to use, clear, concise and efficient

**Technical stack:**
- 100% Clean architecture
- 100% Kotlin
- 100% Flow
- 100% Compose
- Dagger then Koin
- Firebase Realtime Database for 2-way binding
- VivaWallet SDK for bank card reading
- A/B Testing with Firebase
- Crash reporting with Crashlytics

Kadiska has since been acquired by [Netskope](https://www.netskope.com).

Although this is not a professional project, I want to include it among my proudest achievements: my own **fully connected home**. Built on the open-source Home Assistant platform (the largest open-source project by contributor count on GitHub in 2024), I use my technical skills to improve my daily life by scripting and making everything smart — anything that can boost comfort or help save money. Even a 15-year-old pellet stove can be connected if you find the dry contact on the circuit board.

Beyond the comfort it brings, building this solution also let me discover Python building blocks to extract exactly the behaviour I want from Home Assistant for each connected device. I also explored embedded systems and low-level technologies to create my own firmware for ESP32/ESP8266 chips — the basis of many WiFi-connected devices.

Home Assistant is a very rich and complete solution; learning to use it to its full potential is a particularly rewarding challenge.
